C06.reasoning_summary: The customer says he cancelled, but the billing audit log shows no cancellation action was ever recorded, and his only contact was a statement that he was 'thinking of cancelling.' Under Visa 13.2, the merchant wins because no cancellation preceded the 3 Aug 2026 charge.
C06.rule_applied: Under Visa 13.2, the merchant wins if the customer did not cancel before the charge.
C06.economics_note: Full USD 480 is defensible; no partial-delivery issue. Contesting is worth it given the clear audit trail.
C06.draft_response: Snapcast Studio sold Liam Byrne an annual video-editing subscription, renewed on 3 Aug 2026 for USD 480 [Razorpay]. The customer disputes this as a cancelled recurring transaction, claiming 'I cancelled this.' [Razorpay] Our billing audit log records no cancellation action before the renewal [E4]. The customer's only contact on 29 Jul 2026 was a statement that he was 'thinking of cancelling,' to which our agent replied he could cancel from Settings > Billing [E2]. His last login was 28 Jul 2026, and no cancellation was ever recorded [E3]. The terms, accepted 3 Aug 2025, state the subscription renews annually and must be cancelled in Settings > Billing before the renewal date [E1]. Under Visa 13.2, a merchant prevails where the customer did not cancel before the charge, and no cancellation preceded the 3 Aug 2026 renewal [E4]. Attached: terms acceptance record, support chat, login log, and billing audit log [E1][E2][E3][E4].
C06.prevention_tip: When a customer says they are 'thinking of cancelling,' send a confirmation email with a one-click cancel link and a reminder of the next renewal date, so intent is captured in writing.

C15.missing_evidence: Confirmation that J. Whitfield (j.whitfield@gmail.com) was authorised by Acme Holdings Ltd to cancel the booking made by priya.s@acmeholdings.co.uk — e.g. an email from the booker's address (priya.s@acmeholdings.co.uk) confirming the cancellation, or a written authorisation from Acme Holdings Ltd. This determines whether the 1 Mar cancellation is valid and whether a 50% refund (USD 1,600) is due.
C15.reasoning_summary: The cancellation policy was properly disclosed and accepted at checkout, but the cancellation email came from a different person than the booker, and the merchant itself said it only accepts cancellations from the booker. We need to confirm who had authority to cancel before deciding whether a refund is due.
C15.rule_applied: Under 13.7 the merchant wins only if the cancellation policy was properly disclosed and agreed at the time of sale and the customer cancelled outside it; here the policy was agreed, but it is unclear whether the person who cancelled had authority, so the call cannot be made yet.
contradictions: The cancellation email (E2) came from j.whitfield@gmail.com, not from the booker's address priya.s@acmeholdings.co.uk that accepted the terms (E1).
The merchant's own reply (E3) states it only accepts cancellations from the booker, so the 1 Mar cancellation was not validly processed.
C15.economics_note: If the cancellation is confirmed as valid, the policy (E1) allows a 50% refund for a cancellation 10 days before departure, so only USD 1,600 is defensible and USD 1,600 is owed. If the cancellation is not confirmed as valid, the full USD 3,200 is defensible. A lost dispute is clawed back at the dispute-date FX rate and arbitration adds network fees, so confirm authority before contesting.
C15.prevention_tip: Require cancellations to come from the same email address that booked, or add a step where the booker confirms any cancellation request from a different address before it is processed.
